examples.ko: 우리 팀이 내일 준결승전에서 일본 팀과 만나요.
examples.en: Our team plays against Japan in the semifinal tomorrow.

examples.ko: 준결승전 표를 구하려고 아침부터 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: I lined up from the morning to get a semifinal ticket.
Yesterday's semifinal was really nail-biting.
The player who lost in the semifinal shed tears.

examples.ko: 이번 월드컵 준결승전은 몇 시에 시작해요?
examples.en: What time does this World Cup semifinal start?

examples.ko: 친구랑 같이 준결승전을 보러 경기장에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the stadium with a friend to watch the semifinal.

explain: '준결승'이라고만 해도 같은 뜻이라서 대화에서는 짧게 말하기도 해요. 결승 바로 앞 경기라서 '결승전'과 짝으로 외워 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: People often just say '준결승', which means the same thing, so the shorter form is common in conversation. It is the match right before the final, so learn it as a pair with '결승전'.

examples.en: Our school's soccer team was knocked out in the quarterfinal.
From the quarterfinals on, the games get much more intense.
The quarterfinal is held tomorrow afternoon.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 준준결승까지 한 번도 지지 않았어요.
examples.en: That player hadn't lost once until the quarterfinal.
I'm so happy we made it to the quarterfinal.
The quarterfinal results were on the news.

explain: '8강(전)'이라고도 말해요. 준결승 앞 단계라서 '결승 → 준결승 → 준준결승'처럼 '준'이 하나 더 붙는다고 생각하면 쉬워요.
explain_en: It is also called '8강(전)'. Think of it as '준' being added once more at each earlier round: 결승 → 준결승 → 준준결승.

examples.ko: 저는 아직 동호회 준회원이라서 투표를 못 해요.
examples.en: I'm still only an associate member of the club, so I can't vote.
For a month, you take part as an associate member.
Can associate members use the library too?
The joining fee for associate members is cheaper than for full members.
Next month I go from associate member to full member.
To become an associate member, you have to submit documents.

explain: '정회원'의 반대말로 짝지어 외우면 좋아요. '준-'은 정식은 아니지만 그에 가깝다는 느낌을 더해요. 권리가 일부 제한되는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: Learn it as the counterpart of '정회원' (full member). The prefix '준-' adds the sense of 'not fully official, but close'. Often some rights are limited.

examples.ko: 문장 끝에 줄임표를 찍으면 말을 다 안 한 느낌이 나요.
examples.en: If you put an ellipsis at the end of a sentence, it feels like you left something unsaid.
If there are too many ellipses, the writing feels awkward.
You sent only an ellipsis in the message, so I was worried.
Ellipses also appear often in the dialogue of novels.
The writer expressed a hesitant feeling with an ellipsis.
What words might come after the ellipsis?

explain: '마침표', '쉼표'처럼 문장 부호 이름이에요. 말을 줄였거나 망설이는 느낌을 줄 때 써요. 메시지에서는 '점점점'이라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: Like '마침표' and '쉼표', it is the name of a punctuation mark. It suggests words left out or hesitation. In text messages people sometimes call it '점점점' (dot dot dot).

examples.en: You need a tape measure to measure the area of the land.

examples.ko: 줄자를 길게 뽑아서 창문 너비를 쟀어요.
examples.en: I pulled the tape measure out long and measured the window's width.
Could you lend me a tape measure?
The tape measure is in the toolbox.

examples.ko: 이사 가기 전에 줄자로 방 크기를 재야 해요.
examples.en: Before moving, I need to measure the room with a tape measure.
Please take a tape measure along too.

explain: 돌돌 말려 있어서 휘어지는 자예요. 방 크기나 몸 치수처럼 길게 재거나 곡선을 잴 때 편해요. 단단한 직선 자는 그냥 '자'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a coiled ruler that bends. It is handy for measuring long distances, room sizes, body measurements or curves. A rigid straight ruler is just called '자'.

examples.ko: 내일 오전에 팀장님께 중간보고를 해야 해요.
examples.en: I have to give the team leader an interim report tomorrow morning.
Have you finished making the materials for the interim report?
Many problems came up in the interim report.
The project's interim report is next Friday.

examples.ko: 중간보고는 짧게 핵심만 말하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: For an interim report, it's best to say only the key points briefly.
I haven't even given an interim report and the deadline is already here.

explain: 일이 끝나기 전에 진행 상황을 알리는 거라서 끝난 뒤의 '최종 보고'와 짝으로 써요. '중간보고를 하다'라고 하고, 윗사람에게는 '중간보고를 드리다'라고 해요. '중간 보고'처럼 띄어 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It reports progress before the work is done, so it pairs with '최종 보고' (final report). You say '중간보고를 하다', and '중간보고를 드리다' to a superior. It is sometimes written with a space as '중간 보고'.

examples.ko: 집을 계약할 때 중개료를 얼마나 내야 해요?
examples.en: How much do I have to pay as an agent fee when I sign a lease?

examples.ko: 중개료가 너무 비싸서 깎아 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: The agent fee was so expensive that I asked for a discount.
I paid the real estate agency 500,000 won as an agent fee.
The agent fee varies depending on the price of the house.
You should plan your budget with the agent fee in mind too.

examples.ko: 중개료 때문에 직접 거래하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people trade directly because of the agent fee.

explain: 부동산에서는 '중개 수수료'나 '복비'라고 말하기도 해요. '료'는 값을 내는 돈을 나타내서 '수업료', '입장료'와 비슷해요. '중개료를 내다/받다'로 써요.
explain_en: At real estate offices people also say '중개 수수료' or '복비'. The '료' ending marks a fee you pay, like '수업료' or '입장료'. You say '중개료를 내다/받다'.

examples.en: This drama is very popular with middle-aged people.

examples.ko: 중년층을 위한 건강 프로그램이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new health program for the middle aged has started.
These days, middle-aged people use smartphones well too.
Most customers of this shop are middle-aged.

examples.ko: 중년층 취업 문제가 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: The job problems of the middle aged often appear in the news.
The hobbies of middle-aged people have become more varied.

explain: '-층'은 비슷한 나이나 처지의 사람들 무리에 붙어서 '청년층', '노년층'과 함께 써요. 한 사람을 말할 때는 '중년'이라고 해요. 뉴스나 조사 결과에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: The suffix '-층' attaches to a group of people of similar age or situation, as in '청년층' and '노년층'. For one person you say '중년'. You often see it in news and survey results.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 우리 모임에서 중심적 역할을 해요.
examples.en: That person plays a central role in our group.
Many of the central contents come up on the exam.

examples.ko: 이 글에서 중심적이지 않은 부분은 빼도 돼요.
examples.en: You can leave out the parts of this text that aren't central.

examples.ko: 선생님은 그 이야기가 가장 중심적이라고 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher said that story is the most central.

examples.ko: 그 일을 중심적으로 맡은 사람이 누구예요?
examples.en: Who is the person mainly in charge of that work?

examples.ko: 이 단원의 중심적 개념을 먼저 정리해 보세요.
examples.en: First organize the central concepts of this unit.

explain: '중심적 역할'처럼 명사 앞에 오거나 '중심적인', '중심적으로'로 활용해서 써요. '중심이 되는'과 비슷하지만 조금 딱딱한 말투라서 글이나 발표에서 잘 어울려요. '자기중심적'처럼 다른 말과 붙으면 뜻이 달라지니 조심하세요.
explain_en: It comes before a noun, as in '중심적 역할', or is used as '중심적인' or '중심적으로'. It is close to '중심이 되는' but sounds a bit stiff, fitting writing and presentations. Be careful: combined with other words, as in '자기중심적', the meaning changes.

examples.en: My younger sibling is mumbling something to themselves.
Before the test, I memorized words while muttering them.
Why do you keep mumbling to yourself?
Grandfather mumbled in his sleep.
Please don't mumble; speak up.

examples.ko: 그는 화가 났는지 문 앞에서 중얼중얼했어요.
examples.en: He seemed angry and mumbled in front of the door.

explain: 혼잣말이나 불평을 작은 소리로 할 때 써서 듣는 사람이 알아듣기 어렵다는 느낌이 있어요. '중얼거리다'라고도 해요. '중얼중얼'만 부사처럼 써서 '중얼중얼 말하다'라고도 할 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes saying self-talk or complaints in a low voice, with the feeling that listeners can hardly make it out. You can also say '중얼거리다'. The sound word '중얼중얼' alone can act as an adverb, as in '중얼중얼 말하다'.

examples.en: Our company values teamwork.
My parents always value honesty.
More people have come to value their health.
I valued personality more than looks.
There are also companies that don't put weight on experience.
If you value time, prepare in advance.

explain: '중요하게 여기다'와 같은 뜻으로, 중요하게 여기는 것에 '을/를'을 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '중시하다'도 있는데 더 짧고 딱딱해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '중요하게 여기다', and the thing you value takes '을/를'. '중시하다' is a similar word, but shorter and stiffer.

examples.ko: 이 병원에는 중환자가 많아서 늘 바빠요.
examples.en: This hospital has many critical patients, so it's always busy.
The doctor examined the critical patient first.
Visits to critical patients are restricted.
Even family members can't enter the intensive care unit freely.
The nurse is giving medicine to the critical patient.

examples.ko: 중환자 이송 때문에 길이 잠깐 막혔어요.
examples.en: The road was blocked for a moment because of a critical patient's transfer.

explain: '중환자실'이라는 말로 병원 이야기나 드라마에서 자주 들려요. 환자를 높여 말할 때는 보통 '환자분'이라고 해요.
explain_en: You often hear it in the word '중환자실' (intensive care unit) in hospital talk and dramas. To refer to a patient politely, people usually say '환자분'.

examples.en: I set a mousetrap in the kitchen and caught a mouse.
I put cheese in the mousetrap.

examples.ko: 시골집 창고에는 쥐덫이 여러 개 있어요.
examples.en: There are several mousetraps in the country house's storeroom.
Where can I buy a mousetrap?
Grandmother caught the mouse with a mousetrap.
The cat is lingering near the mousetrap.

explain: '쥐덫을 놓다'라고 말해요. '덫에 걸리다'는 비유로 속임수에 빠졌다는 뜻으로도 써요.
explain_en: You say '쥐덫을 놓다' (to set a mousetrap). The phrase '덫에 걸리다' is also used figuratively for falling into a trap or trick.

en: born in the year of the rat

examples.en: My father was born in the year of the rat.
I was born in the same year as my friend who is a rat.
They say people born in the year of the rat are diligent.
My younger sibling is a rat and I'm an ox.
I hear this year is lucky for those born in the year of the rat.
The people born in the year of the rat formed a group.

explain: 한국에서는 '무슨 띠예요?'라고 물으면 '쥐띠예요'처럼 태어난 해의 동물로 대답해요. 다른 띠도 '소띠', '호랑이띠'처럼 '띠'가 붙어요. 나이를 직접 묻지 않고 대략 알아볼 때도 써요.
explain_en: In Korea, when asked '무슨 띠예요?' you answer with your birth-year animal, like '쥐띠예요'. Other signs work the same way, such as '소띠' and '호랑이띠'. People also use it to get a rough idea of someone's age without asking directly.

examples.ko: 마당에 쥐약을 놓았다가 고양이가 먹을까 봐 치웠어요.
examples.en: I put out rat poison in the yard but removed it for fear the cat would eat it.

examples.ko: 쥐약은 위험하니까 아이 손이 닿지 않게 두세요.
examples.en: Rat poison is dangerous, so keep it out of children's reach.
There is rat poison placed in the corner of the storeroom.

examples.ko: 이웃집 강아지가 쥐약 때문에 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: The neighbor's puppy went to the vet because of rat poison.

examples.ko: 쥐약으로 쥐를 잡는 집은 요즘 드물어요.
examples.en: Few households catch mice with rat poison these days.
You must not throw away rat poison carelessly either.

explain: 뜻 그대로는 '쥐약을 놓다'라고 말해요. 친구끼리 하는 말에서는 '나한테 쥐약이야'처럼 비유로도 써요.

phrases.en: Spicy food is poison to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 사람에게 아주 안 좋아서 피해야 하는 것을 말할 때 써요. 편한 대화에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for something very bad for a person that they should avoid. It is casual speech.

explain_en: In its literal sense you say '쥐약을 놓다' (to put out rat poison). Among friends it is also used figuratively, as in '나한테 쥐약이야'.

en: tear at; claw at; pull out

examples.en: I felt so frustrated that I tore at my hair.
The baby cried, clawing at its mother's clothes.
The child was tearing up grass.
The cat clawed the sofa and it became a mess.
Even if you're angry, don't tear at the paper.

examples.ko: 손톱 주변 살을 쥐어뜯는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: I have a habit of picking at the skin around my nails.

explain: 움켜쥐고 세게 잡아당겨 뜯어낼 때 써요. 머리카락, 풀, 옷처럼 붙어 있는 것에 잘 어울려요. 비슷해 보이는 '쥐어짜다'는 꽉 쥐고 짜내는 거라 달라요.

phrases.example: 아들 소식이 없자 어머니는 가슴을 쥐어뜯으며 기다렸어요.
phrases.en: With no news from her son, his mother waited in agony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 괴롭고 답답해서 마음이 아플 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression for being so distressed or frustrated that it hurts emotionally.

explain_en: It means to grab and pull something hard so it tears away, and fits things attached like hair, grass or clothes. The similar-looking '쥐어짜다' is different: it means to squeeze something tightly to wring it out.

examples.en: Customer inquiries need an immediate answer.
This medicine has an immediate effect.
I reacted immediately to that news.

examples.ko: 즉각적이지 않아도 괜찮으니 천천히 답해 주세요.
examples.en: It's fine if it's not immediate, so please answer slowly.

examples.ko: 시민들의 즉각적인 신고로 불이 빨리 꺼졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to citizens' immediate report, the fire was put out quickly.
Please don't expect it to be immediate.

explain: '즉각적인 반응/조치'처럼 '-인'을 붙이거나 '즉각적으로'로 많이 써요. 비슷한 '즉시'는 '즉시 연락 주세요'처럼 바로 부사로 쓰지만, '즉각적'은 그렇게 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '즉각적인' (as in '즉각적인 반응/조치') or '즉각적으로'. The similar '즉시' works directly as an adverb, as in '즉시 연락 주세요', but '즉각적' does not.

examples.en: A forklift is moving cargo in the warehouse.
You need a license to drive a forklift.
It's dangerous to walk in front of a forklift.
My uncle lifted the boxes high with a forklift.

examples.ko: 지게차는 무거운 물건을 들어 올릴 때 써요.
examples.en: A forklift is used when lifting heavy things.
I was almost run over by a forklift and was startled.

explain: 공장이나 창고, 물류센터에서 쓰는 차예요. '지게차를 운전하다'라고 말하고 자격증이 필요해요. 공사장에서 땅을 파는 차(굴착기)와는 달라요.
explain_en: It is a vehicle used in factories, warehouses and logistics centers. You say '지게차를 운전하다', and a license is required. It differs from the digging machine (굴착기) at construction sites.

examples.ko: 길이 지그재그로 나 있어서 천천히 올라갔어요.
examples.en: The road zigzags, so I climbed slowly.
I bought a zigzag-pattern T-shirt.
The mountain road zigzagged, so I felt carsick.
There is a person walking in a zigzag.
Draw the line in a zigzag shape.
The skier comes down in a zigzag.

explain: '지그재그로 걷다/운전하다/그리다'처럼 '로'와 함께 부사처럼 써요. '지그재그 무늬'처럼 명사 앞에도 와요. 이어진 곡선이 아니라 꺾이는 모양이라는 점이 '구불구불'과 달라요.
explain_en: It acts like an adverb with '로', as in '지그재그로 걷다/운전하다/그리다', and also comes before nouns, as in '지그재그 무늬'. Unlike '구불구불' (winding), it has sharp turns rather than smooth curves.

examples.en: The meat is sizzling in the pan.
I like the sound of pork belly sizzling.
Turn down the heat when the oil starts to sizzle.
The frying pan sizzled and a delicious smell came out.
The sausage sizzled on the hot griddle.
The sizzling sound had stopped before I knew it.

explain: 뜨거운 기름이나 불판에서 고기, 전이 익을 때 나는 소리를 나타내서 영어로는 sizzle에 가까워요. 같은 소리를 '지글지글'이라고도 해요. '보글보글'은 찌개처럼 국물이 끓는 소리라서 달라요.
explain_en: It describes the sound of meat or pancakes cooking on hot oil or a griddle, closer to English 'sizzle'. The sound word '지글지글' is the same thing. '보글보글' is different: it is the bubbling of a stew or soup.

examples.en: The meat sizzles as it cooks on the grill.

examples.ko: 지글지글 끓는 찌개를 먹었더니 땀이 났어요.
examples.en: I ate a bubbling-hot stew and started sweating.
It's midday with the sun beating down fiercely.
A sizzling sound is coming from the griddle.
I can hear the sizzle of pancakes frying.

examples.ko: 지글지글 구운 고기에 쌈을 싸 먹었어요.
examples.en: I wrapped the sizzling grilled meat in a leaf and ate it.

explain: 고기 굽는 소리처럼 '지글지글 익다/구워지다'로 써요. '지글지글 끓다'처럼 아주 뜨겁게 끓거나 햇볕이 뜨거운 느낌에도 써요. 동사는 '지글거리다'예요.
explain_en: It is used for sounds like meat grilling, as in '지글지글 익다/구워지다'. It also conveys intense heat, as in '지글지글 끓다' or scorching sunshine. The verb form is '지글거리다'.

examples.en: My head was throbbing, so I took medicine.

examples.ko: 어제 잠을 못 자서 아침부터 머리가 지끈거려요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep yesterday, so my head has been pounding since morning.

examples.ko: 머리가 지끈거리는 걸 보니 감기에 걸렸나 봐요.
examples.en: My head is pounding, so I think I caught a cold.
My head throbbed because of the loud noise.
The throbbing headache has gotten a little better.
If your forehead throbs, rest for a moment.

explain: 머리가 계속 욱신거리며 아플 때 '머리가 지끈거려요'라고 자주 말해요. '머리가 아파요'보다 둔하게 쑤시는 느낌이 있어요. 주어는 보통 아픈 부위(머리, 이마)예요.
explain_en: People often say '머리가 지끈거려요' when their head pounds continuously. Compared with '머리가 아파요', it has a dull, throbbing feel. The subject is usually the aching part, like 머리 or 이마.

examples.en: This winter is terribly cold.
That friend is extremely stubborn.
That person grew up in dire poverty.

examples.ko: 어제 먹은 음식이 지독히 매워서 혼났어요.
examples.en: The food I ate yesterday was awfully spicy and I had a hard time.
That night it rained terribly hard.
It was an unbearably lonely night.

explain: 좋지 않은 정도가 심할 때 써서 추위, 가난, 외로움 같은 부정적인 말과 잘 어울려요. '지독히도'처럼 '도'를 붙이면 더 강조돼요. 형용사는 '지독하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when something bad is extreme, so it goes with negative words like cold, poverty or loneliness. Adding '도', as in '지독히도', adds emphasis. The adjective is '지독하다'.

examples.en: I haven't paid my local taxes yet this year.

examples.ko: 지방세는 구청 홈페이지에서도 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can also pay local taxes on the district office website.
If you buy a car, local taxes are charged.
The local tax bill came by mail.
Can I pay local taxes by card too?

examples.ko: 지방세로 걷은 돈은 지역 도로를 고치는 데 쓰여요.
examples.en: Money collected as local taxes is used to repair local roads.

explain: '국세'와 짝이 되는 말이에요. 자동차세, 재산세처럼 지역에서 걷는 세금이 여기에 들어가요. '지방세를 내다/납부하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It pairs with '국세' (national tax). Taxes collected locally, such as the car tax and property tax, fall under it. You say '지방세를 내다/납부하다'.

en: stay up all night; sit up all night

examples.en: I stayed up all night the night before the exam.
I ended up staying up all night talking with a friend.

examples.ko: 월드컵 경기를 보며 밤을 지새우는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people stay up all night watching World Cup games.
I lie awake all night because of worry.

examples.ko: 밤을 지새우면 다음 날 너무 피곤해요.
examples.en: If you stay up all night, you're very tired the next day.

examples.ko: 오늘은 밤을 지새울 각오로 공부할 거예요.
examples.en: Today I'm going to study ready to stay up all night.

explain: 거의 '밤을 지새우다'처럼 '밤'과 함께 써요. '밤을 새우다'와 비슷하지만 조금 글 같은 말투예요. '지새워요/지새웠어요'로 활용해요.
explain_en: It is almost always used with '밤', as in '밤을 지새우다'. It is close to '밤을 새우다' but sounds a little more literary. It conjugates as '지새워요/지새웠어요'.

examples.en: They say someone made that story up.
The child makes up funny stories.
Don't make up lies.
I made up a reason for being late and told it.
Don't try so hard to come up with an excuse.
Even though it was an invented story, it sounded real.

explain: 없던 이야기나 거짓말을 만들 때 많이 써서 '거짓말, 변명, 이야기'와 잘 어울려요. 소설가가 이야기를 만드는 것에도 써요. '만들어 내다'보다 사실이 아니라는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: It often means making up stories or lies, and goes well with '거짓말', '변명' and '이야기'. It is also used when a novelist creates a story. It carries a stronger sense of 'not true' than '만들어 내다'.

examples.en: Who is the author of this book?

examples.ko: 지은이 이름이 표지에 크게 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The author's name is written large on the cover.
I met the author in person and got an autograph.

examples.ko: 지은이가 쓴 다른 책도 읽어 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to read other books the author wrote too.

examples.ko: 지은이도 이 책이 이렇게 팔릴 줄 몰랐대요.
examples.en: I hear even the author didn't know this book would sell so well.
I sent a thank-you letter to the author.

explain: 책 표지나 목록에서 '지은이 ○○'처럼 써요. '저자', '작가'와 같은 뜻으로 쓸 수 있지만 순우리말이라 부드러운 느낌이에요. 그림은 '그린이', 번역은 '옮긴이'라고 해요.
explain_en: It appears on book covers and listings as '지은이 ○○'. It can be used like '저자' or '작가', but as a native Korean word it feels softer. The illustrator is '그린이' and the translator is '옮긴이'.

examples.en: I made small animals with paper clay with my child.
Paper clay gets hard when it dries.

examples.ko: 미술 시간에 지점토를 사 오라고 했어요.
examples.en: They told us to buy paper clay for art class.
A lot of paper clay got on my hands.
I painted the paper clay doll with paint.
Can I buy paper clay at a stationery store too?

explain: 종이로 만든 가벼운 점토라서 흙으로 만든 찰흙과 달리 마르면 단단해져요. 학교 미술 시간이나 만들기에서 만날 수 있어요. '지점토로 만들다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is a light clay made from paper, and unlike ordinary earth clay (찰흙) it hardens as it dries. You may meet it in school art class and crafts. You say '지점토로 만들다'.
